A Lifetime Love Affair With Les Boys

May 14, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

How does a girl from Saskatchewan become a lifelong fan of the Montreal Canadiens? Growing up the closest team to my hometown was the Winnipeg Jets so proximity wasn’t a factor. When I was in Kindergarten, Gretzky and the Oilers began their dynasty of Cup runs. Like my classmates I idolized The Great One but I’m not the bandwagon jumping type.* To the best of my remembrance, the origins my fandom was a mixture of early childhood rebellion, logic and a belief in destiny.

Rebellion My parents cheered for the Toronto Maple Leafs** and I wasn’t about to cheer for a team just because they did. I remember very distinctly cheering for the Habs during the 1986 Stanley Cup finals while everyone else I knew cheered for the Calgary Flames. I remember feeling so smug when the Canadiens won. Three years later, I cried when Montreal lost to Calgary (cementing my lifelong hatred for the Flames).

Logic When I was young, my parents used to take us to Regina Pats games. Outside the entrance to the rink you can read about the team’s history. When I learned that the Pats used to be a Montreal Canadiens farm team, it made me feel like the Habs were my home team. Once waiting to get into the rink, an old-timer told me that Montreal was the greatest team ever. They had won the Stanley Cup more times than anyone else so it seemed to be sound logic.

Destiny This last one might seem a little silly. I was born during the 1978 Stanley Cup playoffs and one month later Montreal won the Cup. This was a team with passionate fans where history and tradition are of the utmost importance – my kind of people. My little kid logic thought this meant this was the team I was supposed to cheer for.

*Was also ridiculed in elementary school for not being a Def Leopard fan or New Kids on the Block fan. Further proof that I had excellent taste from a young age. ** I have since shown them the error of their ways. —
